'''Dogecoin''' ({{IPAc-en|'|d|oʊ|(|d|)|ʒ|k|ɔɪ|n}} {{Respell|DOHJ|koyn}} or {{Respell|DOHZH|koyn}},<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailydot.com/unclick/how-to-say-dogecoin-pronunciation/|title=How do you pronounce 'Dogecoin'?|date=April 24, 2014|website=The Daily Dot|language=en|access-date=December 21, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181222082001/https://www.dailydot.com/unclick/how-to-say-dogecoin-pronunciation/|archive-date=December 22, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> [[ISO 4217#Cryptocurrencies|Abbreviation]]:  '''DOGE'''; [[Currency symbol|sign]]: '''Ð''') is a [[cryptocurrency]] created by software engineers Billy Markus and Jackson Palmer, who decided to create a payment system as a joke, making fun of the wild speculation in cryptocurrencies at the time.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.barrons.com/articles/dogecoin-started-as-a-joke-now-its-too-important-to-laugh-off-51620229273|title=Dogecoin Started as a Joke. Now It's Too Important to Laugh Off|website=Barrons|access-date=May 12, 2021|archive-date=May 13, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210513164106/https://www.barrons.com/articles/dogecoin-started-as-a-joke-now-its-too-important-to-laugh-off-51620229273|url-status=live}}</ref> It is considered both the first "[[meme coin]]", and more specifically the first "dog coin". Despite its satirical nature, some consider it a legitimate investment prospect. Dogecoin features the face of [[Kabosu (dog)|Kabosu]] from the "[[Doge (meme)|doge]]" [[internet meme|meme]] as its logo and namesake.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Roose |first1=Kevin |title=Is There a Cryptocurrency Bubble? Just Ask Doge |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=September 15, 2017 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/09/15/business/cryptocurrency-bubble-doge.html |issn=0362-4331  |access-date=October 3, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171003125659/https://www.nytimes.com/2017/09/15/business/cryptocurrency-bubble-doge.html |archive-date=October 3, 2017 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="A History of Dogecoin.">[https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3091219 ''A History of Dogecoin'']. {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180603102446/https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3091219 |date=June 3, 2018 }}. Dogecoin Analysis Report. Social Science Research Network (SSRN). Accessed December 28, 2017.</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.digitaltrends.com/social-media/wow-dogecoin-bitcoin/| title=Wow. Dogecoin is the most Internet thing to happen, ever.| first=Andrew| last=Couts| publisher=[[Digital Trends]]| date=December 12, 2013| access-date=December 12, 2013| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131214025357/http://www.digitaltrends.com/social-media/wow-dogecoin-bitcoin/| archive-date=December 14, 2013| url-status=live}}</ref> It was introduced on December&nbsp;6, 2013, and quickly developed its own [[online community]], reaching a peak market capitalization of over US$85&nbsp;billion{{Efn|US$85,314,347,523.}} on May&nbsp;5, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|first=Stephen|last=Hutcheon|title=The rise and rise of dogecoin, the internet's hottest cryptocurrency|url=https://www.smh.com.au/technology/technology-news/the-rise-and-rise-of-dogecoin-the-internets-hottest-cryptocurrency-20140124-31d24.html|work=Sydney Morning Herald|access-date=April 5, 2014|date=January 24, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140331045048/http://www.smh.com.au/technology/technology-news/the-rise-and-rise-of-dogecoin-the-internets-hottest-cryptocurrency-20140124-31d24.html|archive-date=March 31, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> As of 2021, it is the [[shirt sponsor|sleeve sponsor]]{{Efn|Sleeve only.}} of [[Watford Football Club]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Watford FC to feature Doge on football shirts|url=https://www.cityam.com/watford-fc-doge/|website=CityAM|date=August 16, 2021|access-date=August 18, 2021|archive-date=August 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210828174013/https://www.cityam.com/watford-fc-doge/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Dogecoin.com promotes the currency as the "fun and friendly Internet currency", referring to its origins as a "joke".<ref>{{cite web |title=What is Dogecoin and what does it have to do with Elon Musk and Saturday Night Live? |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-05-10/what-is-dogecoin-elon-musk-saturday-night-live/100128024 |work=Australian Broadcasting Corporation |access-date=May 10, 2021 |date=May 9, 2021 |archive-date=April 5, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230405014349/https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-05-10/what-is-dogecoin-elon-musk-saturday-night-live/100128024 |url-status=live }}</ref> Software engineers Markus and Palmer launched the satirical cryptocurrency as a way to make fun of [[Bitcoin]] and the many other cryptocurrencies boasting grand plans to take over the world. Dogecoin quickly gained traction, particularly on social platforms like [[Reddit]]. Within two weeks of launch, it had established a dedicated blog and forum and its market value reached $8&nbsp;million, once jumping to become the seventh largest electronic currency in the world.<ref name="cnbc 2021-05-07">{{Cite web|last=Sigalos|first=MacKenzie|date=May 7, 2021|title=How dogecoin went from a joke to one of the world's top cryptocurrencies|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/05/07/what-is-dogecoin.html|access-date=July 12, 2021|website=CNBC|language=en|archive-date=July 10, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210710153452/https://www.cnbc.com/2021/05/07/what-is-dogecoin.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==History==
Originally formed as a joke,<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|date=February 11, 2021|title=Dogecoin's Creator Is Baffled by Meteoric Rise to $9 Billion|language=en|work=Bloomberg.com|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-02-11/dogecoin-s-creator-is-just-as-baffled-as-you-are-about-its-rise|access-date=February 12, 2021|archive-date=February 12, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210212223741/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-02-11/dogecoin-s-creator-is-just-as-baffled-as-you-are-about-its-rise|url-status=live}}</ref> Dogecoin was created by [[IBM]] software engineer Billy Markus and [[Adobe Inc.|Adobe]] software engineer Jackson Palmer. They wanted to create a [[peer-to-peer]] digital currency that could reach a broader demographic than [[Bitcoin]]. In addition, they wanted to distance it from the controversial history of other coins.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/dogecoins-founders-believe-in-the-power-of-meme-currencies/|title=Such Weird: The Founders of Dogecoin See the Meme Currency's Tipping Point|date=December 23, 2013|publisher=[[Vice Media]]|first=Patrick|last=McGuire|work=Motherboard|access-date=December 23, 2013|archive-date=September 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170922051212/https://motherboard.vice.com/en_us/article/dogecoins-founders-believe-in-the-power-of-meme-currencies|url-status=live}}</ref> Dogecoin was officially launched on December 6, 2013, and within the first 30 days, there were over 1 million visitors to Dogecoin.com.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://junkee.com/an-interview-with-the-inventor-of-dogecoin-the-internets-favourite-new-currency/27411 |title=An Interview With The Creator Of Dogecoin: The Internet's Favourite New Currency |last=Noyes |first=Jenny |date=January 22, 2014 |website=[[Junkee]] |publisher=[[Junkee Media]] |access-date=January 12, 2021 |quote="Jackson Palmer accidentally invented Dogecoin in early December ... within the first 30 days there were over a million visitors to Dogecoin.com." |archive-date=January 24, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140124233428/https://junkee.com/an-interview-with-the-inventor-of-dogecoin-the-internets-favourite-new-currency/27411 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Palmer is credited with making the idea a reality. At the time, he was a member of the Adobe marketing department in [[Sydney, Australia|Sydney]], Australia, while Markus was a senior software engineer at IBM in [[Portland, Oregon]].<ref name=whatisdogecoin>{{cite web| url=http://www.businessinsider.com/what-is-dogecoin-2013-12| title=What is Dogecoin?| first=Rob| last=Wile| work=[[Business Insider]]| date=December 19, 2013| access-date=December 19, 2013| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131220072107/http://www.businessinsider.com/what-is-dogecoin-2013-12| archive-date=December 20, 2013| url-status=live}}</ref> Palmer had purchased the domain Dogecoin.com and added a [[splash screen]], which featured the coin's logo and scattered [[Comic Sans]] text. Markus reached out to Palmer after seeing the site, and started efforts to develop the currency. Markus designed Dogecoin's protocol based on existing cryptocurrencies Luckycoin and [[Litecoin]],<ref name="suchvalue2" /> which use [[scrypt]] technology in their [[proof-of-work]] algorithm.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.seattlepi.com/technology/heavy/article/Dogecoin-5-Fast-Facts-You-Need-to-Know-5079680.php|title=Dogecoin: 5 Fast Facts You Need to Know|newspaper=Seattle Post-Intelligencer |date=December 10, 2013|access-date=February 16, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221232623/http://www.seattlepi.com/technology/heavy/article/Dogecoin-5-Fast-Facts-You-Need-to-Know-5079680.php|archive-date=February 21, 2014|url-status=live |last1=Vega |first1=Danny }}</ref> The use of scrypt means that miners cannot use [[SHA-2|SHA-256]] bitcoin mining equipment, and instead must use dedicated [[field-programmable gate array]] and [[application-specific integrated circuit]] devices for mining which are known to be more complex to produce.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.dailydot.com/business/shibe-meme-dogecoin-currency/| title=With its own cryptocurrency, Doge has officially conquered 2013| first=Miles| last=Klee| publisher=[[The Daily Dot]]| date=December 10, 2013| access-date=December 10, 2013| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140123002054/http://www.dailydot.com/business/shibe-meme-dogecoin-currency/| archive-date=January 23, 2014| url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Why Bitcoin mining has a finite cap, and Dogecoin mining doesn't |url=https://www.dailydot.com/business/dogecoin-no-mining-limit-infinite/ |website=The Daily Dot |language=en |date=February 5, 2014 |access-date=September 21, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190921025115/https://www.dailydot.com/business/dogecoin-no-mining-limit-infinite/ |archive-date=September 21, 2019 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On December 19, 2013, Dogecoin jumped nearly 300% in value in 72 hours, rising from $0.00026 to $0.00095,<ref name="suchvalue">{{cite web| url=http://www.digitaltrends.com/cool-tech/dogecoin-price-value-jump-bitcoin| title=To the moon! DogeCoin fetches 300 percent jump in value in 24 hours.| first=Andrew| last=Couts| publisher=[[Digital Trends]]| date=December 19, 2013| access-date=December 19, 2013| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219222007/http://www.digitaltrends.com/cool-tech/dogecoin-price-value-jump-bitcoin/| archive-date=December 19, 2013| url-status=live}}</ref> with a volume of billions of Dogecoins traded per day. This growth occurred during a time when Bitcoin and many other cryptocurrencies were reeling from China's decision to forbid Chinese banks from investing in the Bitcoin economy.<ref name="suchvalue2">{{cite web| url=http://www.ibtimes.co.uk/what-dogecoin-meme-that-became-hot-new-virtual-currency-1429847| title=What is Dogecoin? The Meme that Became the Hot New Virtual Currency.| first=David| last=Gilbert| work=[[International Business Times]]| date=December 20, 2013| access-date=December 20, 2013| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906080317/http://www.ibtimes.co.uk/what-dogecoin-meme-that-became-hot-new-virtual-currency-1429847| archive-date=September 6, 2015| url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Dogecoin experienced its first major crash when its price dropped by 80% due to this event and to large [[mining pool]]s exploiting the small amount of computing power required at the time to mine Dogecoin.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.businessinsider.com/dogecoin-crashed-this-weekend-2013-12| title=Dogecoin Prices Crashed This Weekend| first=Rob| last=Wile| work=[[Business Insider]]| date=December 22, 2013| access-date=December 22, 2013| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131223223048/http://www.businessinsider.com/dogecoin-crashed-this-weekend-2013-12| archive-date=December 23, 2013| url-status=live}}</ref>

On December 25, 2013, the first major theft of Dogecoin occurred when millions of coins were stolen during a [[Hack (computer security)|hack]] on the online [[cryptocurrency wallet]] platform Dogewallet.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://gizmodo.com/millions-of-meme-based-dogecoins-stolen-on-christmas-da-1489819762| title=Millions of Meme-Based Dogecoins Stolen on Christmas Day| first=Ashley| last=Feinberg| publisher=[[Gizmodo]]| date=December 26, 2013| access-date=December 26, 2013| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131226230149/http://gizmodo.com/millions-of-meme-based-dogecoins-stolen-on-christmas-da-1489819762| archive-date=December 26, 2013| url-status=live}}</ref> According to the platform's management, the hacker, having gained access to the platform, redirected all transactions to a single [[Cryptocurrency wallet|wallet address]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://techcrunch.com/2013/12/25/dogecoin-hack/| title=Such Hack. Many Dogecoin. Very Disappear. So Gone. Wow.| first=Catherine| last=Shu| publisher=[[TechCrunch]]| date=December 25, 2013| access-date=December 25, 2013| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131227001014/http://techcrunch.com/2013/12/25/dogecoin-hack/| archive-date=December 27, 2013| url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.latimes.com/business/technology/la-fi-tn-dogecoin-theft-currency-bitcoin-20131226,0,2575238.story#axzz2ojLWuO2X| title=Millions of Dogecoins, currency based on a meme, are reported stolen| first=Salvador| last=Rodriguez| work=[[Los Angeles Times]]| date=December 26, 2013| access-date=December 26, 2013| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131227004821/http://www.latimes.com/business/technology/la-fi-tn-dogecoin-theft-currency-bitcoin-20131226,0,2575238.story#axzz2ojLWuO2X| archive-date=December 27, 2013| url-status=live}}</ref> This hacking incident spiked tweets about Dogecoin, making it the most mentioned altcoin on [[Twitter]] at the time, although it was in reference to a negative event. To help those who lost funds on Dogewallet after its breach, the Dogecoin community started an initiative named "SaveDogemas" to help donate coins to those who had them stolen. Approximately one month later, enough money was donated to cover all of the coins that were stolen.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.digitaltrends.com/cool-tech/dogecoin-dogewallet-hack-save-dogemas/|title=Such generosity! After Dogewallet heist, Dogecoin community aims to reimburse victims|date=December 27, 2013|access-date=March 2, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140227152856/http://www.digitaltrends.com/cool-tech/dogecoin-dogewallet-hack-save-dogemas/|archive-date=February 27, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>

In January 2014, the trading volume of Dogecoin briefly surpassed that of all other cryptocurrencies combined. However, its market capitalization remained substantially behind that of Bitcoin. Initially, Dogecoin featured a randomized reward that is received for each mining block. However, in March 2014, this behaviour was updated to a static block reward.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dogecoin: The meme that got serious :: InBlog|url=https://inblog.in/Dogecoin-The-meme-that-got-serious-2xmkzoHRt2|access-date=November 15, 2021|website=inblog.in|language=en|archive-date=November 15, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211115131734/https://inblog.in/Dogecoin-The-meme-that-got-serious-2xmkzoHRt2|url-status=dead}}</ref>
Co-founder Jackson Palmer left the cryptocurrency community in 2015<!--<ref name=":0"/>--> and has no plans to return, having come to the belief that cryptocurrency, originally conceived as a libertarian alternative to money, is fundamentally exploitative and built to enrich its top proponents. His co-founder, Billy Markus, agreed that Palmer's position was generally valid.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Murphy |first1=Mike |title=Dogecoin co-creator blasts crypto as a scam to help the rich get richer |work=MarketWatch |date=July 14, 2021 |url=https://www.marketwatch.com/story/dogecoin-co-creator-blasts-crypto-as-a-scam-to-help-the-rich-get-richer-11626310808 |language=EN-US |access-date=July 20, 2021 |archive-date=July 20, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210720225405/https://www.marketwatch.com/story/dogecoin-co-creator-blasts-crypto-as-a-scam-to-help-the-rich-get-richer-11626310808 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Locke |first1=Taylor |title=The co-creator of dogecoin explains why he doesn't plan to return to crypto: It's 'controlled by a powerful cartel of wealthy figures' |work=CNBC |date=July 14, 2021 |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/07/14/dogecoin-co-creator-jackson-palmer-criticizes-the-crypto-industry.html |language=en |access-date=July 20, 2021 |archive-date=July 19, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210719044112/https://www.cnbc.com/2021/07/14/dogecoin-co-creator-jackson-palmer-criticizes-the-crypto-industry.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

During the 2017 to early 2018 [[cryptocurrency bubble]], Dogecoin briefly reached a peak of $0.017 on January 7, 2018, putting its total market capitalization near $2&nbsp;billion.

In July 2020, the price of Dogecoin spiked following a [[TikTok]] trend aimed at getting Dogecoin to $1.<ref>{{cite web|last=Winck|first=Ben|date=July 8, 2020|title=Dogecoin volumes spike 683% after viral TikTok challenge urges buying spree|url=https://markets.businessinsider.com/currencies/news/dogecoin-price-volumes-skyrocket-viral-tiktok-buying-spree-cryptocurrency-market-2020-7-1029377900#|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200709174155/https://markets.businessinsider.com/currencies/news/dogecoin-price-volumes-skyrocket-viral-tiktok-buying-spree-cryptocurrency-market-2020-7-1029377900|archive-date=July 9, 2020|access-date=July 9, 2020|website=Business Insider}}</ref>

On May 9, 2021, [[SpaceX]] announced a rideshare mission to the Moon completely funded by Dogecoin, thus becoming the first space mission funded by a cryptocurrency. [[Elon Musk]] confirmed this news via Twitter.<ref>{{cite news |date=May 10, 2021 |title=Dogecoin used to pay for SpaceX's mission to the moon next year |agency=Al Jazeera |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2021/5/10/dogecoin-used-to-pay-for-spacexs-mission-to-the-moon-next-year |access-date=May 10, 2021 |archive-date=December 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211213200628/https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2021/5/10/dogecoin-used-to-pay-for-spacexs-mission-to-the-moon-next-year |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Doge-1|DOGE-1]], a [[CubeSat]], was planned to be a minor 40&nbsp;kg rideshare payload on [[Intuitive Machines]]' [[IM-1]] mission in Q1 2022,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Geometric Energy press release |title=SpaceX to Launch DOGE-1 to the Moon! |url=https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/spacex-to-launch-doge-1-to-the-moon--875845973.html |access-date=May 10, 2021 |website=www.newswire.ca |language=en |archive-date=May 17, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210517033102/https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/spacex-to-launch-doge-1-to-the-moon--875845973.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=May 9, 2021 |title=SpaceX accepts dogecoin as payment to launch lunar mission next year |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/spacex-accepts-dogecoin-payment-launch-lunar-mission-next-year-2021-05-09/ |access-date=May 10, 2021 |website=Reuters |archive-date=May 9, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210509234004/https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/spacex-accepts-dogecoin-payment-launch-lunar-mission-next-year-2021-05-09/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=IM-1 Nova-C & DOGE-1 |url=https://nextspaceflight.com/launches/details/1915 |access-date=May 9, 2021 |website=NextSpaceflight |archive-date=January 19, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230119112757/https://nextspaceflight.com/launches/details/1915 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sheetz |first=Michael |date=May 9, 2021 |title=SpaceX accepts Dogecoin as payment to launch 'DOGE-1 mission to the Moon' next year |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/05/09/spacex-accepts-dogecoin-payment-for-doge-1-mission-to-the-moon.html |website=CNBC |access-date=May 9, 2021 |archive-date=December 5, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211205220122/https://www.cnbc.com/2021/05/09/spacex-accepts-dogecoin-payment-for-doge-1-mission-to-the-moon.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=May 10, 2021 |title=We knew @ElonMusk was taking #Dogecoin to the Moon, but had no idea it would be on our flight. |url=https://twitter.com/Int_Machines/status/1391843506193326092 |access-date=May 10, 2021 |website=Twitter |archive-date=May 10, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210510195212/https://twitter.com/Int_Machines/status/1391843506193326092 |url-status=live }}</ref> but ultimately was delayed to a potential later mission.{{Citation needed|date=June 2024}}

On August 14, 2021, the Dogecoin Foundation announced the "re-establishment of the Dogecoin Foundation (est 2014), with a renewed focus on supporting the Dogecoin Ecosystem, Community and promoting the future of the Dogecoin [[Blockchain]]."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dogecoin Foundation |date=August 16, 2021 |title=Announcement: Re-establishing the Dogecoin Foundation |url=https://foundation.dogecoin.com/posts/2021/08/announcement-re-establishing-the-dogecoin-foundation/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210817164020/https://foundation.dogecoin.com/posts/2021/08/announcement-re-establishing-the-dogecoin-foundation/ |archive-date=August 17, 2021 |access-date=September 30, 2021 |website=Dogecoin Foundation |language=en}}</ref> The Foundation was reinvigorated by the addition to its Board of notable advisors such as [[Vitalik Buterin]] ([[Ethereum]] co-founder and inventor) and [[Jared Birchall]] (representing Elon Musk).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kiderlin |first=Sophie |date=August 18, 2021 |title=Ethereum co-creator Vitalik Buterin will help shape the future of dogecoin after joining the token's foundation ===2021 boom===
In January 2021, Dogecoin went up over 800% in 24 hours, reaching $0.07, as a result of attention from [[Reddit]] users, partially encouraged by Elon Musk and the [[GameStop short squeeze]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kharpal |first1=Arjun |title=Reddit frenzy pumps up Dogecoin, a cryptocurrency started as a joke, by over 800% |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/money/companies/reddit-frenzy-pumps-up-dogecoin-a-cryptocurrency-started-as-a-joke-by-over-800/ar-BB1dc4sw |access-date=January 29, 2021 |agency=CNBC |archive-date=February 5, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210205064539/https://www.msn.com/en-us/money/companies/reddit-frenzy-pumps-up-dogecoin-a-cryptocurrency-started-as-a-joke-by-over-800/ar-BB1dc4sw |url-status=live }}</ref> In February 2021, Dogecoin hit a new high price of $0.08 following Twitter encouragement from Musk, [[Snoop Dogg]] and [[Gene Simmons]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Yang |first1=Yueqi |title=Dogecoin Soars to New Record as Musk Fires off New Tweet |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-02-07/dogecoin-soars-again-toward-record-after-crashing-last-week |access-date=February 21, 2021 |work=[[Bloomberg News|Bloomberg]] |date=February 7, 2021 |language=en |archive-date=February 23, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210223064213/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-02-07/dogecoin-soars-again-toward-record-after-crashing-last-week |url-status=live }}</ref> In March 2021, [[Dallas Mavericks]] owner [[Mark Cuban]] announced his [[NBA]] team would allow purchasing tickets and products with Dogecoin; within two days, Cuban had declared his franchise had become the top Dogecoin merchant, having carried out 20,000 transactions.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Baer |first1=Jack |title=Mark Cuban boasts Mavericks are largest Dogecoin merchant in the world |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/mark-cuban-mavericks-largest-dogecoin-merchant-cryptocurrency-021811555.html |website=[[Yahoo! Sports]] |access-date=April 17, 2021 |date=March 6, 2021 |archive-date=May 20, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210520235200/https://sports.yahoo.com/mark-cuban-mavericks-largest-dogecoin-merchant-cryptocurrency-021811555.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

In April 2021, Dogecoin and other cryptocurrencies surged, stimulated in part by the [[direct listing]] for cryptocurrency exchange [[Coinbase]] on April 14, although that platform did not provide trading of Dogecoin.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ostroff |first1=Caitlin |title=Bitcoin and Dogecoin Prices Soar to Records Ahead of Coinbase Listing |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/cryptocurrencies-soar-to-records-ahead-of-coinbase-listing-11618400809 |website=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |access-date=April 14, 2021 |date=April 14, 2021 |archive-date=May 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506190151/https://www.wsj.com/articles/cryptocurrencies-soar-to-records-ahead-of-coinbase-listing-11618400809 |url-status=live }}</ref> Dogecoin first reached $0.10 on April 14,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Madhok |first1=Diksha |title=Dogecoin price surpasses 10 cents to reach an all-time high |url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/04/14/tech/dogecoin-crypocurrency-intl-hnk/index.html |website=[[CNN]] |access-date=April 14, 2021 |location=New Delhi |date=April 14, 2021 |archive-date=May 10, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210510085915/https://www.cnn.com/2021/04/14/tech/dogecoin-crypocurrency-intl-hnk/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref> before hitting a new high of $0.45 on April 16 (up 400% that week<ref name="CNBC 2021-04-16" />), with a volume of nearly $70 billion traded in the preceding 24 hours.<ref name="MW 2021-04-17">{{cite web |last1=DeCambre |first1=Mark |title=This dogecoin chart offers the clearest explanation for the buzz surrounding the 'joke' crypto |url=https://www.marketwatch.com/story/this-dogecoin-chart-offers-the-clearest-explanation-for-the-buzz-surrounding-the-joke-crypto-11618597012 |website=[[MarketWatch]] |access-date=April 17, 2021 |date=April 17, 2021 |archive-date=May 5, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210505105155/https://www.marketwatch.com/story/this-dogecoin-chart-offers-the-clearest-explanation-for-the-buzz-surrounding-the-joke-crypto-11618597012 |url-status=live }}</ref> {{as of|2021|04|alt=At the time}}, Dogecoin's market capitalization approached $50 billion, making it the fifth-highest-valued cryptocurrency;<ref>{{cite web |last1=Goldman |first1=David |title=What is Dogecoin? How a joke became hotter than bitcoin |url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/04/17/investing/what-is-dogecoin/index.html |website=[[CNN]] |access-date=April 17, 2021 |date=April 17, 2021 |archive-date=May 5, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210505013419/https://www.cnn.com/2021/04/17/investing/what-is-dogecoin/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref> its value had increased more than 7,000% per year to-date.<ref name="MW 2021-04-17" /> Interest in Dogecoin contributed to an outage in electronic trading platform [[Robinhood (company)|Robinhood]]'s cryptocurrency system on April 15, caused by "unprecedented demand", and prompted concerns from experts of a nearing [[speculative bubble]] in the cryptocurrency market.<ref name="CNBC 2021-04-16">{{cite web |last1=Browne |first1=Ryan |title=Dogecoin spikes 400% in a week, stoking fears of a cryptocurrency bubble |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/04/16/dogecoin-doge-price-meme-cryptocurrencys-rise-sparks-bubble-fears.html |website=[[CNBC]] |access-date=April 17, 2021 |date=April 16, 2021 |archive-date=May 5, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210505163301/https://www.cnbc.com/2021/04/16/dogecoin-doge-price-meme-cryptocurrencys-rise-sparks-bubble-fears.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

On May 4, 2021, the value of Dogecoin first surpassed the symbolic hurdle of $0.50.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Pound|first=Jesse|date=May 4, 2021|title=Dogecoin surges 30% to a record above 50 cents as speculative crypto trading continues|work=CNBC|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/05/04/dogecoin-surges-above-50-cents-to-record-as-speculative-crypto-trading-continues.html|access-date=May 15, 2021|archive-date=June 15, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220615172823/https://www.cnbc.com/2021/05/04/dogecoin-surges-above-50-cents-to-record-as-speculative-crypto-trading-continues.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

In April 2023, a Dogecoin increase was attributed to Elon Musk temporarily changing the logo on the Twitter app to a Doge logo.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kolodny |first=Rohan Goswami, Lora |date=2023-04-03 |title=Dogecoin jumps more than 30% after Musk changes Twitter logo to image of shiba inu |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2023/04/03/dogecoin-jumps-over-30percent-after-twitter-changes-logo-to-doges-symbol.html |access-date=2023-07-17 |website=CNBC |language=en |archive-date=July 17, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230717181934/https://www.cnbc.com/2023/04/03/dogecoin-jumps-over-30percent-after-twitter-changes-logo-to-doges-symbol.html |url-status=live }}</ref>  In June 2023, Musk was accused of insider trading by investors based on a series of stunts including the change of logo.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2023/jun/01/elon-musk-insider-trading-dogecoin-lawsuit|title=Elon Musk accused of insider trading in Dogecoin lawsuit|newspaper=The Guardian |date=June 2, 2023 }}</ref>

On August 29, 2024, Elon Musk and his electric vehicle company [[Tesla, Inc.|Tesla]] won the dismissal of a federal lawsuit accusing them of defrauding investors by hyping the cryptocurrency dogecoin and conducting insider trading, causing billions of dollars of losses.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-30 |title=Musk Dodges Legal Bullet: Manhattan Judge Dismisses $258 Billion Lawsuit Over Dogecoin Claims - TechGyve |url=https://techgyve.com/musk-dodges-legal-bullet-manhattan-judge-dismisses-258-billion-lawsuit-over-dogecoin-claims/ |access-date=2024-08-31 |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Use and exchanges==
Dogecoin is an altcoin{{Efn|A slang term in the [[cryptocurrency]] and technology media and community for an alternate cryptocurrency, or, de facto, any [[cryptocurrency]] other than [[Bitcoin]].}} with a large userbase, and is traded against both [[fiat currencies]] and other cryptocurrencies on several reputable [[cryptocurrency]] exchanges and retail investment platforms.

Trading physical, tangible items in exchange for Dogecoin takes place on online communities such as Reddit and Twitter, where users in such circles frequently share cryptocurrency-related information.<ref name="A History of Dogecoin." /><ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.theverge.com/2013/12/16/5216862/bitcoin-is-so-2013-dogecoin-is-new-crypto-currency-on-the-block| title=Bitcoin is so 2013: Dogecoin is the new cryptocurrency on the block| first=Nathan| last=Ingraham| publisher=[[The Verge]]| date=December 16, 2013| access-date=December 16, 2013| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131217012230/http://www.theverge.com/2013/12/16/5216862/bitcoin-is-so-2013-dogecoin-is-new-crypto-currency-on-the-block| archive-date=December 17, 2013| url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.complex.com/tech/2013/12/dogecoin-on-reddit| title=Move Over Bitcoin: Dogecoin is Here| author=J. Duaine Hahn| publisher=Complex Tech| date=December 16, 2013| access-date=December 16, 2013| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219100220/http://www.complex.com/tech/2013/12/dogecoin-on-reddit| archive-date=December 19, 2013| url-status=live}}</ref>

Cases of people using their employers'{{Which|date=December 2024}} or universities' computers to mine Dogecoin have been discovered including a Harvard community member and a student at London's [[Imperial College London|Imperial College]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Hutchinson|first1=Lee|title=Harvard supercomputing cluster hijacked to produce dumb cryptocurrency|url=https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2014/02/harvard-supercomputing-cluster-hijacked-to-produce-alt-cryptocurrency/|access-date=June 13, 2014|work=Ars Technica|publisher=Condé Nast|date=February 21, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140621135131/http://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2014/02/harvard-supercomputing-cluster-hijacked-to-produce-alt-cryptocurrency/|archive-date=June 21, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Hern|first1=Alex|title=Student uses university computers to mine Dogecoin|url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2014/mar/04/dogecoin-bitcoin-imperial-college-student-mine|access-date=June 13, 2014|work=The Guardian|date=March 4, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140713213709/http://www.theguardian.com/technology/2014/mar/04/dogecoin-bitcoin-imperial-college-student-mine|archive-date=July 13, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>

Dogecoin has been used in an attempted property sale,<ref>{{cite news|last=Imam|first=Jareen|title=Man selling home for $135,000 in Dogecoins|url=http://www.cnn.com/2014/02/26/tech/innovation/dogecoin-cryptocurrency-tech-irpt/|publisher=CNN|access-date=March 17, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140318031220/http://www.cnn.com/2014/02/26/tech/innovation/dogecoin-cryptocurrency-tech-irpt/|archive-date=March 18, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> and it has been used in the pornography<ref>{{cite news|title=Fox on Reddit: Porn star looks to accept virtual currency Dogecoin|url=http://www.foxnews.com/tech/2014/02/27/fox-on-reddit-porn-star-looks-to-accept-virtual-currency-on-website/|access-date=March 17, 2014|newspaper=FoxNews.com|date=February 27, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140310123307/http://www.foxnews.com/tech/2014/02/27/fox-on-reddit-porn-star-looks-to-accept-virtual-currency-on-website/|archive-date=March 10, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> and gambling{{Efn|Primarily [[poker]].}} industries.

===Online tipping===
One major mainstream commercial application of the cryptocurrency has been Internet-based tipping systems, in which social media users tip other users for providing interesting or noteworthy content.<ref>{{cite web|date=January 24, 2014|title=The rise and rise of the Dogecoin and internet tipping culture|url=https://www.abc.net.au/pm/content/2013/s3931812.htm|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150403004949/http://www.abc.net.au/pm/content/2013/s3931812.htm|archive-date=April 3, 2015|access-date=March 4, 2015|publisher=Australian Broadcasting Corporation}}</ref>

====Dogetipbot====
Dogetipbot was a cryptocurrency transaction service used on popular sites like Reddit and [[Twitch (service)|Twitch]]. It allowed users to send Dogecoins to other users through commands via Reddit comments. In May 2017, Dogetipbot was discontinued and taken offline after its creator declared bankruptcy; this left many Dogetipbot users losing their coins stored in the Dogetipbot system.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gizmodo.com/reddit-users-lose-real-money-after-meme-currency-bot-di-1795125165|title=Reddit Users Lose Real Money After Meme Currency Bot Dies|first=Peter|last=Yeh|publisher=[[Gizmodo]]|date=May 11, 2017|access-date=September 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170908052407/http://gizmodo.com/reddit-users-lose-real-money-after-meme-currency-bot-di-1795125165|archive-date=September 8, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Smart contracts==
Dogecoin's blockchain cannot interact with [[smart contract]]s directly. Dogecoin can be tied to the Ethereum blockchain in order to access some [[decentralized finance]] (DeFi) instruments.{{citation needed|date=May 2024}}

==Currency supply==
Dogecoin started with an intended supply limit of Ð100&nbsp;[[billion]], which would have been far more coins than the top digital currencies were then allowing. By mid-2015, the 100 billionth Dogecoin had been mined, with an additional Ð5&nbsp;billion put into circulation every year thereafter. In February 2014, Palmer announced that the limit would not be added in the codebase in an effort to create a consistent inflation rate over time.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dogecoin to allow annual inflation of 5 billion coins each year, forever|date=February 3, 2014|url=https://arstechnica.com/business/2014/02/dogecoin-to-allow-annual-inflation-of-5-billion-coins-each-year-forever/|publisher=Ars Technica|access-date=February 4, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140204051957/http://arstechnica.com/business/2014/02/dogecoin-to-allow-annual-inflation-of-5-billion-coins-each-year-forever/|archive-date=February 4, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Mining parameters==
Dogecoin's implementation differs from its predecessors: It was originally [[Fork (blockchain)|forked]] from [[Litecoin]], then refactored to Bitcoin. Dogecoin's target block time is 1 minute, as opposed to Litecoin's 2.5 minutes and Bitcoin's 10 minutes.<ref name="A History of Dogecoin."/>

==Fundraising==
===2014 Winter Olympics===

The Dogecoin community and foundation have encouraged fundraising for charities and other notable causes. On January 19, 2014, a fundraiser was established by the Dogecoin community to raise $50,000 for the [[Jamaican Bobsled Team]], which had qualified for, but could not afford to go to, the [[Sochi Winter Olympics]]. By the second day, $36,000 worth of Dogecoin was donated and the Dogecoin to Bitcoin exchange rate rose by 50%.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Rodriguez|first1=Salvador|title=Jamaican bobsled team boosts value of Dogecoin, currency based on meme|url=https://www.latimes.com/business/technology/la-fi-tn-jamaican-bobsled-dogecoin-currency-meme-20140120-story.html|work=Los Angeles Times|date=January 20, 2014|access-date=February 21, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200211215434/https://www.latimes.com/business/technology/la-fi-tn-jamaican-bobsled-dogecoin-currency-meme-20140120-story.html|archive-date=February 11, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>  The Dogecoin community also raised funds for a second Sochi athlete, [[Shiva Keshavan]].<ref>{{cite web |first=Devin |last=Coldewey |url=http://www.nbcnews.com/technology/dogecoin-cryptocurrency-donors-help-send-indian-athletes-sochi-2D12024654 |title=Dogecoin cryptocurrency donors help send Indian athletes to Sochi |publisher=NBC News.com |date=January 29, 2014 |access-date=February 2, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202003942/http://www.nbcnews.com/technology/dogecoin-cryptocurrency-donors-help-send-indian-athletes-sochi-2D12024654 |archive-date=February 2, 2014 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Doge4Water===
In 2014, The Dogecoin Foundation, led by [[Eric Nakagawa]], began collecting donations to build a well in the Tana river basin in Kenya for  [[World Water Day]] (March 22). The campaign, in cooperation with [[Charity: Water]], collected donations from more than 4,000 donors, including one anonymous benefactor who donated 14,000,000 dogecoin (worth approximately $11,000 at the time), raising over US$30,000.<ref>{{cite web |first=David |last=Gilbert |url=http://www.ibtimes.co.uk/most-valuable-tweet-history-donates-11000-worth-dogecoin-kenyan-water-charity-1440565 |title='Most Valuable Tweet in History' Donates $11,000 Worth of Dogecoin to Kenyan Water Charity |publisher=IB Times |date=March 17, 2014 |access-date=May 25, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714140736/http://www.ibtimes.co.uk/most-valuable-tweet-history-donates-11000-worth-dogecoin-kenyan-water-charity-1440565 |archive-date=July 14, 2014 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===NASCAR===
[[File:Josh Wise Sonoma 2014.jpg|thumb|left|[[Josh Wise]]'s Dogecoin-sponsored Chevrolet in 2014]]
On March 25, 2014, the Dogecoin community successfully raised Ð67.8&nbsp;million (around US$55,000 at the time) in an effort to sponsor [[NASCAR]] [[Sprint Cup Series]] driver [[Josh Wise]]. Nicknamed the "Moonrocket",<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2014/mar/27/nascar-dogecoin-sponsor-josh-wise-talladega-superspeedway |title=Dogecoin raises $55,000 to sponsor Nascar driver |last=Hern |first=Alex |date=March 27, 2014 |work=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=January 12, 2021 |quote="Named the "#98 Moonrocket", the car will make its debut on May 4th at the Aarons 499 Sprint Series Cup Race."}}</ref> the No. 98 car featured a Dogecoin/Reddit-sponsored paint scheme and was driven by Wise at the [[2014 Aaron's 499|Aaron's 499]] at [[Talladega Superspeedway]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Estrada|first=Chris|url=http://motorsportstalk.nbcsports.com/2014/03/25/nascar-fans-on-reddit-use-dogecoin-to-sponsor-josh-wise/|title=NASCAR fans on Reddit use DogeCoin to sponsor Josh Wise|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|date=March 26, 2014|access-date=March 26, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140326115450/http://motorsportstalk.nbcsports.com/2014/03/25/nascar-fans-on-reddit-use-dogecoin-to-sponsor-josh-wise/|archive-date=March 26, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> Wise and the car were featured for nearly a minute, during which the race commentators discussed Dogecoin and the crowdfunding effort, while finishing twentieth and narrowly avoiding multiple wrecks.<ref name="Dogecar Highlights">{{cite web|last=Stuckey|first=Daniel|title=Talladega Shibe: The Dogecar's NASCAR Highlights|date=May 5, 2014 |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/talladega-shibe-josh-wises-highlights-in-the-dogecar/|access-date=May 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140506050130/http://motherboard.vice.com/read/talladega-shibe-josh-wises-highlights-in-the-dogecar|archive-date=May 6, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>[[File:Josh Wise (19675077586).jpg|thumb|Josh Wise 2015 Chevrolet DogeCoin racecar]]
On May 16, 2014, Wise won a spot at the [[2014 NASCAR Sprint All-Star Race|Sprint All-Star Race]] through an online fan vote beating [[Danica Patrick]], largely due to the efforts of the Dogecoin Reddit community. He finished the race in fifteenth, the last car running.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nascar/2014/05/16/josh-wise-beats-danica-patrick-in-all-star-race-fan-vote-dogecoin/9197981/|title=Josh Wise wins fan vote, beats Danica Patrick|first=Mike|last=Hembree|date=May 16, 2014|access-date=May 18, 2014|newspaper=USA Today|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140518010525/http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nascar/2014/05/16/josh-wise-beats-danica-patrick-in-all-star-race-fan-vote-dogecoin/9197981/|archive-date=May 18, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Polygon">{{Cite news|url=http://www.polygon.com/2014/5/18/5728334/dogecoin-nascar-video-game-dlc|title=Dogecoin, NASCAR's strangest hood sponsor, will appear in its official video game|publisher=Polygon|first=Owen S.|last=Good|date=May 18, 2014|access-date=May 18, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140518210248/http://www.polygon.com/2014/5/18/5728334/dogecoin-nascar-video-game-dlc|archive-date=May 18, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Eutechnyx]], the developer of the ''[[NASCAR '14]]'' video game, added the Dogecoin car as a drivable car in a [[Downloadable content|DLC]] pack.<ref name="Polygon"/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2014/04/24/tech/web/nascar-dogecoin-talladega/|title=Reddit, Dogecoin support NASCAR racer at Talladega|date=April 24, 2014|access-date=May 18, 2014|publisher=CNN|first=Larry|last=Frum|quote=Fans of the NASCAR '14 video game will also get the chance to race the Dogecoin car for themselves when it is added in an upcoming DLC pack. In fact, they have featured the scheme on a DLC pack that costs $0.99 on the Xbox 360 and the Xbox One.|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140519022456/http://edition.cnn.com/2014/04/24/tech/web/nascar-dogecoin-talladega/|archive-date=May 19, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2021, Dogecoin co-sponsored the No. 99 [[NASCAR Xfinity Series]] car of [[B. J. McLeod Motorsports]] in the [[NASCAR Xfinity Series at Las Vegas (spring race)|Alsco Uniforms 300]] at [[Las Vegas Motor Speedway|Las Vegas]]. The car was driven by [[Stefan Parsons]], whose father [[Phil Parsons]] ran [[Phil Parsons Racing]] that fielded Wise's No. 98, with additional backing from Springrates.<ref>{{cite news|last=Haas|first=Jared|url=https://frontstretch.com/2021/03/02/stefan-parsons-dogecoin-sponsorship/|title=Much Wow: Dogecoin Returns to NASCAR on Stefan Parsons' Car|publisher=Frontstretch|date=March 2, 2021|access-date=February 3, 2025}}</ref>

==Sports ownership==
In Summer 2025, it was announced that House of Doge, an investment arm of Dogecoin, had become the largest equity holder in Italian soccer team [[US Triestina Calcio 1918]].<ref name="pr-tri25">{{cite press release | title =US Triestina Calcio 1918 Welcomes House of Doge as Largest Equity Holder | location=Trieste | publisher =US Triestina Calcio 1918 | date =September 12, 2025 | url =https://www.triestina1918.it/en/club-news/533/us-triestina-calcio-1918-welcomes-house-of-doge-as-largest-equity-holder | access-date =June 3, 2026}}</ref> Shortly after, it became the second largest investor in Swiss ice hockey team [[HC Sierre]].<ref>{{cite web | url =https://www.lenouvelliste.ch/valais/valais-central/sierre-district/sierre-commune/hc-sierre-dogecoin-la-crypto-preferee-delon-musk-investit-en-valais-1473438 |title =HC Sierre: Dogecoin, la crypto préférée d’Elon Musk, investit en Valais  |last1 =De Iaco |first1 =Didier |date =October 29, 2025 |work =[[Le Nouvelliste (Switzerland)|Le Nouvelliste]] |language =fr | access-date =June 3, 2026}}</ref><ref name="pr-sier26">{{cite press release | title =The Dogecoin Hockey Team – HC Sierre – Win the 2025–26 Sky Swiss League Championship | location=New York; Miami | publisher =House of Doge; Brag House Holdings | date =April 9, 2026 | url =https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/dogecoin-hockey-team-hc-sierre-win-2025-26-sky-swiss-league-championship-2026-04-09 | access-date =June 3, 2026}}</ref>

In Spring 2026, House of Doge became the main investor in [[Milano Hockey Club]], an expansion [[ICE Hockey League]] team with plans to begin operations in the 2026–27 season.<ref>{{cite web |url =https://milano.corriere.it/notizie/cronaca/26_giugno_02/milano-hockey-club-ammesso-all-ice-hockey-league-dopo-due-decenni-sul-ritorno-nella-lega-internazionale-centrato-l-obiettivo-0f46b252-dc76-4e0e-9a53-10058ab4exlk_amp.shtml |title =Milano Hockey Club ammesso all'Ice Hockey League: dopo due decenni sul ritorno nella lega internazionale. 'Centrato l'obiettivo fissato dopo le Olimpiadi' |last1 =Riggio |first1 =Salvatore |date =June 2, 2026 |work =Corriere della serra |language =it |access-date =June 3, 2026}}</ref><ref name="pr-mhc26">{{cite press release | title =House of Doge Celebrates Winning The Milano Hockey Club Franchise Approval and Admission to the ICE Hockey League for the 2026/27 Season  | location=New York; Miami | publisher =House of Doge; Brag House Holdings | date =June 2, 2026 | url =https://www.stocktitan.net/news/TBH/house-of-doge-celebrates-winning-the-milano-hockey-club-franchise-orcrk04zq4kj.html | access-date =June 3, 2026}}</ref>

==Criticism==
Dogecoin's origin as a "joke", which makes it the first [[meme coin]], has made it difficult to be taken seriously by mainstream media and financial experts.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnet.com/news/dogecoin-the-origin-story-of-the-elon-musk-supported-cryptocurrency/|title=Dogecoin: Inside the joke cryptocurrency that somehow became real|first=Mark|last=Serrels|website=CNET|access-date=May 12, 2021|archive-date=November 3, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211103012216/https://www.cnet.com/news/dogecoin-the-origin-story-of-the-elon-musk-supported-cryptocurrency/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fortune.com/2020/07/09/what-is-dogecoin-tiktok-crypto/|title=What is Dogecoin?|website=Fortune|access-date=May 12, 2021|archive-date=May 24, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230524174430/https://fortune.com/2020/07/09/what-is-dogecoin-tiktok-crypto/|url-status=live}}</ref> The cryptocurrency has had a long and problematic history of scams.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://foreignpolicy.com/2021/02/11/dogecoin-how-does-it-work-elon-musk-cryptocurrency/|title=Confused About Dogecoin? Here's How It (Doesn't) Work.|first=David|last=Gerard|date=February 11, 2021|access-date=May 12, 2021|archive-date=April 5, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230405191431/https://foreignpolicy.com/2021/02/11/dogecoin-how-does-it-work-elon-musk-cryptocurrency/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.news18.com/news/tech/dogecoin-has-a-warning-for-everyone-do-not-fall-for-scams-that-promise-to-double-your-coins-3722831.html|title=Dogecoin Has A Warning For Everyone: Do Not Fall For Scams That Promise To Double Your Coins|date=May 10, 2021|website=www.news18.com|access-date=May 12, 2021|archive-date=April 5, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230405092739/https://www.news18.com/news/tech/dogecoin-has-a-warning-for-everyone-do-not-fall-for-scams-that-promise-to-double-your-coins-3722831.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/dogecoin-my-joke-cryptocurrency-hit-2-billion-jackson-palmer-opinion/|title=My Joke Cryptocurrency Hit $2 Billion and Something Is Very Wrong|website=Vice.com|date=January 11, 2018|access-date=May 12, 2021|archive-date=May 26, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230526050156/https://www.vice.com/en/article/9kng57/dogecoin-my-joke-cryptocurrency-hit-2-billion-jackson-palmer-opinion|url-status=live}}</ref> Similar to many other cryptocurrencies, Dogecoin has been described by some commentators as a form of [[Ponzi scheme|Ponzi]] scheme. Critics allege that Dogecoin investors who purchased Dogecoins early on, have a large financial incentive to draw others into purchasing more Dogecoins in order to drive the price up, therefore benefitting the early investors financially at the direct expense of later purchasers.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Kelly|first=Jemima|date=May 11, 2021|title=Dogecoin gives away the crypto game|url=https://www.ft.com/content/2c3dd96c-b1b1-42fd-ab46-8b4791bf1270|website=Financial Times|access-date=May 12, 2021|archive-date=May 24, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230524055056/https://www.ft.com/content/2c3dd96c-b1b1-42fd-ab46-8b4791bf1270|url-status=live}}</ref> This is primarily because Dogecoin does not have a supply cap like other cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin, which has a capped supply of 21 million coins.<ref name="cnbc 2021-05-07"/>

==Elon Musk and Dogecoin==
[[Elon Musk]] frequently uses his [[Twitter|X]] platform to express his views on Dogecoin, which has led some to claim that his actions amount to [[market manipulation]] because the price of Dogecoin frequently experiences price movements shortly after his tweets.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Stempel |first=Jonathan |date=2023-06-01 |title=Elon Musk is accused of insider trading by investors in Dogecoin lawsuit |url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/elon-musk-is-accused-insider-trading-by-investors-dogecoin-lawsuit-2023-06-01/ |access-date=2025-02-09 |work=Reuters}}</ref> Nevertheless, because cryptocurrencies are not regulated like stocks, these actions are not illegal.<ref>{{Cite web|date=May 14, 2021|title=How murky legal rules allow Tesla's Elon Musk to keep moving markets|url=https://www.livemint.com/market/cryptocurrency/how-murky-legal-rules-allow-tesla-s-elon-musk-to-keep-moving-markets-11621009061887.html|access-date=August 22, 2021|website=mint|language=en|archive-date=August 22, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210822120722/https://www.livemint.com/market/cryptocurrency/how-murky-legal-rules-allow-tesla-s-elon-musk-to-keep-moving-markets-11621009061887.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Musk and his promotion of Dogecoin have been criticized by Dogecoin co-founder Jackson Palmer, who called Musk a "self-absorbed [[Confidence trick|grifter]]".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Massie |first1=Graeme |title=Co-creator of Dogecoin lashes out at 'self-absorbed grifter' Elon Musk over bitcoin stand |url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/co-creator-dogecoin-lashes-self-233410149.html |work=[[The Independent]] |via=[[Yahoo! Finance]] |access-date=12 April 2022 |date=14 May 2021 |archive-date=April 12, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220412062957/https://finance.yahoo.com/news/co-creator-dogecoin-lashes-self-233410149.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Musk's first Dogecoin-related tweet occurred on December 20, 2020. Musk tweeted "One Word: Doge". Shortly after, the value of Dogecoin rose by 20%.<ref name="Chris Isidore">{{Cite web|author=Chris Isidore|title=Elon Musk tweeted. Dogecoin surged more than 50%|url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/02/04/investing/elon-musk-dogecoin/index.html|access-date=July 29, 2021|website=CNN|date=February 4, 2021|archive-date=July 29, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210729143802/https://www.cnn.com/2021/02/04/investing/elon-musk-dogecoin/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref> This was followed by a series of Dogecoin-related tweets by Musk in early February 2021 captioned "Dogecoin is the people's crypto" and "no highs, no lows, only Doge". Following these tweets, the value of Dogecoin rose by roughly 40%.<ref name="Chris Isidore"/>

On April 15, 2021, the price of Dogecoin rose by more than 100% after Musk tweeted an image of [[Joan Miró]]'s [[Dog Barking at the Moon (Miró)|''Dog Barking at the Moon'' painting]] captioned "Doge Barking at the Moon",<ref>{{Cite web|author=Diksha Madhok|title=Dogecoin price hits an all-time high after Elon Musk's tweet|url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/04/16/investing/dogecoin-price-elon-musk-int-hk/index.html|access-date=July 29, 2021|website=CNN|date=April 16, 2021|archive-date=July 29, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210729123016/https://www.cnn.com/2021/04/16/investing/dogecoin-price-elon-musk-int-hk/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref> a message which was taken by some as a reference to the industry slang term "to the moon",<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lopatto |first1=Elizabeth |title=Dogecoin is on a run, has escaped the yard, and is headed to the moon |url=https://www.theverge.com/2021/4/16/22387486/dogecoin-run-valuation-cryptocurrency-spike-elon-musk |access-date=4 April 2023 |work=The Verge |date=16 April 2021 |archive-date=April 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230404121120/https://www.theverge.com/2021/4/16/22387486/dogecoin-run-valuation-cryptocurrency-spike-elon-musk |url-status=live }}</ref> meaning a hoped-for increase in a cryptocurrency's value.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rossolillo |first1=Nicholas |title=What Does 'To The Moon' Mean in Cryptocurrency? |url=https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/market-sectors/financials/cryptocurrency-stocks/to-the-moon-crypto/ |access-date=4 April 2023 |work=The Motley Fool |language=en |archive-date=April 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230404121120/https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/market-sectors/financials/cryptocurrency-stocks/to-the-moon-crypto/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On May 8, 2021, Dogecoin fell as much as 29.5%, dropping to US$0.49 during Musk's ''[[Saturday Night Live]]'' appearance.<ref>{{Cite web|author=MacKenzie Sigalos|title=Dogecoin plunges nearly 30% during Elon Musk's SNL appearance|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/05/08/dogecoin-price-plummets-as-elon-musk-hosts-saturday-night-live-.html|access-date=August 17, 2022|website=CNBC|date=May 9, 2021|archive-date=August 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220816213924/https://www.cnbc.com/2021/05/08/dogecoin-price-plummets-as-elon-musk-hosts-saturday-night-live-.html|url-status=live}}</ref> It then rose by 11% on May 20, 2021, shortly after Musk tweeted a Doge-related [[meme]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Pound|first=Jesse|date=May 20, 2021|title=Dogecoin jumps after series of Elon Musk tweets fans more wild cryptocurrency trading|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/05/20/dogecoin-jumps-on-elon-musk-tweet-as-wild-cryptocurrency-trading-continues.html|access-date=July 4, 2021|website=CNBC|language=en|archive-date=July 3, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210703202139/https://www.cnbc.com/2021/05/20/dogecoin-jumps-on-elon-musk-tweet-as-wild-cryptocurrency-trading-continues.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In the same month, the price of Dogecoin was up 10% in the hours after Musk tweeted a Reddit link for users to submit proposals to improve the cryptocurrency.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Browne |first=Ryan |date=December 14, 2021 |title=Dogecoin spikes more than 20% after Elon Musk says Tesla will accept it as payment for merch |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/12/14/dogecoin-price-surges-after-elon-musk-tweet-about-tesla-merch.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214134550/https://www.cnbc.com/2021/12/14/dogecoin-price-surges-after-elon-musk-tweet-about-tesla-merch.html |archive-date=December 14, 2021 |access-date=December 14, 2021 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref>

On December 14, 2021, Dogecoin spiked more than 20% after Musk said that [[Tesla, Inc.|Tesla]] will accept the currency as a means of payment for Tesla merchandise.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite news|date=|title=Elon Musk says Tesla will accept dogecoin as payment for merchandise, touts its value for transactions|work=Marketwatch|url=https://www.marketwatch.com/story/elon-musk-says-tesla-will-accept-dogecoin-as-payment-for-merchandise-touts-its-value-for-transactions-11639505240|access-date=December 15, 2021|archive-date=December 15, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211215165231/https://www.marketwatch.com/story/elon-musk-says-tesla-will-accept-dogecoin-as-payment-for-merchandise-touts-its-value-for-transactions-11639505240|url-status=live}}</ref>

On June 16, 2022, Elon Musk was named in a complaint seeking damages of $258 billion. The complaint was filed in federal court in Manhattan by plaintiff Keith Johnson. Johnson cited Musk's repeated use of his massive social influence to promote the [[altcoin]], which he claims artificially inflated the price.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2022-06-16|title=Elon Musk sued for $258 billion over alleged Dogecoin pyramid scheme|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/elon-musk-sued-258-billion-over-alleged-dogecoin-pyramid-scheme-2022-06-16/|access-date=June 21, 2022|archive-date=June 21, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220621203850/https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/elon-musk-sued-258-billion-over-alleged-dogecoin-pyramid-scheme-2022-06-16/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Prior to [[Acquisition of Twitter by Elon Musk|Musk's acquisition of Twitter]], he had suggested that Dogecoin could be used for Twitter transactions, such as the purchase of [[Twitter#X Premium (formerly Twitter Blue)|Twitter Blue]] accounts.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Zeitchik |first=Steven |date=November 7, 2022 |title=Musk sees a big role for crypto on Twitter. He'll face a tall climb. |newspaper=The Washington Post |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2022/11/07/elon-musk-sees-crypto-larger-part-twitter-its-steep-climb/ |access-date=November 14, 2022 |archive-date=November 16, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221116073429/https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2022/11/07/elon-musk-sees-crypto-larger-part-twitter-its-steep-climb/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On October 27, 2022, Elon Musk completed a deal to take Twitter private. This led to a sustained rise in the price of Dogecoin from October 25 to October 29, with Dogecoin increasing as much as 46%.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sigalos |first=MacKenzie |date=2022-10-27 |title=Dogecoin surges 35% as Elon Musk's Twitter deal approaches close |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2022/10/27/dogecoin-surges-40percent-as-elon-musks-twitter-deal-approaches-close.html |access-date=2023-10-28 |website=CNBC |language=en |archive-date=October 28, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231028093405/https://www.cnbc.com/2022/10/27/dogecoin-surges-40percent-as-elon-musks-twitter-deal-approaches-close.html |url-status=live }}</ref> When X announced the launch of its X Money Account digital wallet product in February 2025, cryptocurrencies were not supported.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mattson |first=Jennifer |date=2025-01-28 |title=Elon Musk's X partners with Visa to move into financial services—and no, it's not for crypto (yet) |url=https://www.fastcompany.com/91268412/x-visa-partnership-financial-services-payments-crypto-elon-musk |access-date=2025-02-13 |work=[[Fast Company]]}}</ref>

Between April 3 and April 7,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gizmodo.com/twitter-removes-doge-icon-dogecoin-price-falls-1850311581|title=Doge's Twitter Reign Ends, Triggering Memecoin Slump|accessdate=April 8, 2023|date=April 7, 2023|work=Gizmodo|last=Leffer|first=Lauren|archive-date=April 8, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230408064007/https://gizmodo.com/twitter-removes-doge-icon-dogecoin-price-falls-1850311581|url-status=live}}</ref> 2023, Twitter's bird logo was replaced with an image of the [[Doge meme]] for desktop users, leading to a rise in Dogecoin prices.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Clark |first1=Mitchell |title=Today in Twitter: where are the retweet labels, and why did Doge replace the bird? |url=https://www.theverge.com/2023/4/3/23668356/twitter-doge-bird-logo-retweet-labels-following-timeline |access-date=3 April 2023 |archive-date=June 2, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230602172422/https://www.theverge.com/2023/4/3/23668356/twitter-doge-bird-logo-retweet-labels-following-timeline |url-status=live }}</ref> No reason was given for the icon change, with some speculating that it was a late [[April Fool's joke]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=Taylor |first1=Josh |title=Twitter changes logo to Dogecoin cryptocurrency image in apparent late April fool's day gag |url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2023/apr/04/twitter-changes-logo-to-dogecoin-cryptocurrency-image-in-apparent-late-april-fools-day-gag |access-date=4 April 2023 |work=The Guardian |date=4 April 2023 |archive-date=May 24, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240524080857/https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2023/apr/04/twitter-changes-logo-to-dogecoin-cryptocurrency-image-in-apparent-late-april-fools-day-gag |url-status=live }}</ref> or an attempt to [[trolling|troll]] investors over the Dogecoin lawsuit that Musk was seeking to end that week.<ref>{{cite news |title=Twitter is covered in Doge for no discernible reason |url=https://www.engadget.com/twitter-is-covered-in-doge-for-no-discernible-reason-192552749.html |access-date=4 April 2023 |work=Engadget |archive-date=April 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230404121120/https://www.engadget.com/twitter-is-covered-in-doge-for-no-discernible-reason-192552749.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

On November 14, 2024, president-elect [[Donald Trump]] announced that [[Elon Musk]] and [[Vivek Ramaswamy]] would lead a new [[Department of Government Efficiency]] or DOGE for short, an acronym that shares the name of Dogecoin. The price of Dogecoin spiked soon after.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Macheel |first=Tanaya |date=2024-11-13 |title=Dogecoin spikes after Trump announces a Department of Government Efficiency — DOGE |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2024/11/13/dogecoin-surges-20percent-after-trump-announces-a-department-of-government-efficiency-doge.html |access-date=2024-12-10 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref>
